subject: POC final readout scheduling & decision \u2014 Veridian Bio
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Patel <sanjay.patel@veridianbio.com>, Linda Gomez <linda.gomez@veridianbio.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-01T15:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: POC planning — Veridian Bio / Redwood

Hi Sanjay / Linda,

Great to meet today — thanks for the time. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth for the POC planning: 

Summary of what we discussed:
- Goal: Validate Redwood inference for Veridian Bio’s internal document summarization pipeline and clinical note embeddings at production latency/cost targets.
- Scope: 2-week trial against a representative subset (~25k tokens/day) with both summarization and embedding endpoints.

Proposed success criteria (please confirm):
1) Latency: 95th pctile end-to-end generation latency < 800ms for summary requests at 512 token context.
2) Quality: ROUGE-L / internal QA pass rate >= 85% vs. your baseline summarization model on the 200-case eval set.
3) Cost: Per-token inference cost <= $0.004 at expected throughput after batching (we'll show cost estimates).

Evaluation plan / owners:
- Redwood (Marcus): model configuration, test harness, metrics collection (inference latency, token counts, failure rates).
- Veridian (Sanjay): ground-truth eval set, access to test S3 bucket, executive reviewer for final readout.
- Veridian (Linda): procurement + contract point-of-contact.

Timeline (draft):
- Week of Sep 6: Test dataset handoff and connectivity checks.
- Week of Sep 13: POC execution (2 full business days of steady-state testing; burst testing as requested).
- Sep 15–16: Final readout to Veridian execs (go/no-go decision).

Attachments: VERIDIAN_POC_PLAN_v2.pdf (full test plan) attached.

Ask: Can you confirm the success criteria above and whether Sep 15 or Sep 16 would work for the final readout? Also confirm who will be the executive decision maker for the go/no-go.

Thanks — I’ll loop Marcus in for the tech runbook once we lock dates.

Best,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0199

Subject: Re: POC planning — Veridian Bio / Redwood

Thanks Marissa — useful recap. A few notes from our side: 

1) Success criteria: the latency target looks good; on quality we’ll run the 200-case eval plus an additional 50 case sample from our recent trials. Our internal threshold is effectively a 10% uplift in summarization F1 vs our legacy model, so if you can map ROUGE-L to that we’ll be able to sign off.

2) Procurement: I’ve CC’d procurement — they’ll need an SOW + a rough cost estimate to route this for a PO.

3) Security: Our InfoSec team will want SOC2 docs and a short note on how you handle PII during the POC. Can you include a one-page security summary?

4) Exec timing: Our product exec (Eva Martinez) has a review window on Sep 16 afternoon (PST) — that might be the safer go/no-go. Could we target Sept 16 for the readout? If Redwood prefers Sep 15 we’ll need to confirm exec availability.

If you can send a SOW draft and the security note I’ll push procurement and InfoSec in parallel.

—Sanjay
Sanjay Patel
Head of ML Platform | Veridian Bio
sanjay.patel@veridianbio.com

Hi all — quick tech notes ahead of the dataset handoff: 

- Test harness: I’ll provision a dedicated POC endpoint on our dedicated pool to ensure consistent latency. We’ll enable continuous batching and prefix caching; for reproducibility we’ll pin the model to rwinf/gpt-medium-qa:2026-07-01.
- Metrics: dashboard will report per-request latency (p50/p95/p99), tokens in/out, failure rate, and summary quality (ROUGE-L, F1 mapped from your sample labels).
- Test data: please upload the eval set to the shared S3 folder (see Drive link) and provide read-only credentials. We’ll run an initial connectivity check on Sep 9.
- Measurement methodology: we’ll run three steady-state runs (8 hours each) to capture variance and one burst test to evaluate tail latency under load.

I’ll prepare a short runbook (POC_test_data_manifest.csv) with file-level expectations and the exact load profile.

—Marcus
Principal Infra Engineer | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com
